payload.review_scope: final uncommitted opt-in R81 measured-transition selection preparation

resolved_findings.evidence: The plan now replays the actual predecessor ensemble and production arm selector, binds exact ordered manifest rows plus physical float32 pattern hashes, and rejects a same-pool substitution after all caller-controlled hashes are recomputed.

Transition use is independently detected from the complete bound controller tree and later-row provenance; omission of transition_selection_receipts now rejects and forces the transition runtime producer set.
Canonical plan path, pre-state hash, input path, input manifest hash, arm counts, and post-state hash are recomputed and compared rather than trusted from the self-hashed receipt.

Current lifecycle state now requires the frozen top-level schema, exact contiguous batch range and next_batch, measured_budget equality, exact per-batch field schemas, physical input binding, predecessor model lineage, and validated feedback/model evidence.

The final exact-row patch compares each entire manifest row with its canonical production row, so an arbitrary soft_target or other extra truth alias rejects even after manifest, state, and receipt hashes are recomputed.

verified_properties: The soft 0.1 dB preference remains bounded and applies only to authenticated measured parents; candidate scoring and five-margin SM output are unchanged.
The deterministic pool remains 1024 unique candidates with 512 fresh and 512 parent variants, 32 geometry-first parents, and the existing 20/20/20 later-arm quotas.
Fresh and mutated candidates carry no measured truth fields; parent variants retain only a narrow provenance reference, and the exact row schema rejects added truth aliases.

Frozen state, dataset rows, prior feedback, prior models, implementation sources, selector sources, model files, candidate pool, exact selected bundle, and physical pattern bytes are replayed or hash-bound.

The initial state is an exact successor. Later lifecycle state is narrow and contiguous. The completion receipt is last, existing receipts are never overwritten, and finalize is the explicit recovery path after state publication.
Transition receipt/source/runtime closure is opt-in but cannot be downgraded by omitting the receipt field once transition evidence or row provenance exists.
The ordinary exploration defaults and native R80 validation path remain unchanged by the opt-in call sites reviewed here.

remaining_limits.title: Cross-host exact CPU prediction replay is unverified
remaining_limits.detail: Plan regeneration stores raw CPU ensemble prediction and uncertainty floats and requires exact plan equality. Different worker hosts, Torch builds, BLAS implementations, or thread schedules may produce tiny float differences even when candidate IDs, arm assignments, and model bytes agree. No actual three-host replay evidence exists.
remaining_limits.required_before_release: Run the committed, Git-bound receipt validator on all three intended worker environments against the same frozen evidence and confirm byte-identical plan replay, or explicitly revise the receipt contract to bind stable selection decisions without claiming unverified raw-float portability. This review does not choose or validate a numerical relaxation.

remaining_limits.title: Preparation is uncommitted
remaining_limits.detail: The runtime validator requires committed Git blobs and a clean path binding. A real validate_release execution cannot truthfully pass against these uncommitted files.
